problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ of the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{n}}{(3n)!}=1-\frac{x}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{6!}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9!}+⋯\,.
$$
worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{n}}{(3n)!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n+1}}{(3n+3)!}\cdot \frac{(3n)!}{(-1)^{n}{x}^{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{-x(3n)!}{(3n+3)!}| \\  & =|-x|\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(3n)!}{(3n+3)!} \\  & =|x|\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(3n)!}{(3n)!(3n+1)(3n+2)(3n+3)} \\  & =|x|\cdot {lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{(3n+1)(3n+2)(3n+3)} \\  & =|x|\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty .$
